text:
alex: Hi @maria — I see you opened a ticket about embeddings failing with a dimension mismatch when calling /v1/embeddings. Can you paste the exact request body and the error you get?

maria: Thanks Alex. Here's the failing payload (redacted):
```json
{
  "model": "open-embed-medium-1024",
  "input": ["example sentence", "another one"],
  "batch_size": 8
}
```
Response: 400 Bad Request
```
{
  "error": "dimension_mismatch: expected embedding dim 1536 but got 1024"
}
```
I thought open-embed-medium was 1024 dims? Not sure why Redwood expects 1536.

alex: Good catch. Two quick possibilities: 1) model name mapping on our side changed and we're routing that model name to a different variant (1536), or 2) the customer's client or SDK is defaulting to a different model. Can you confirm which model the account was provisioned to use?

maria: It's a self-serve account, no pin. We called model: open-embed-medium-1024 explicitly. SDK was a direct HTTP curl call.

jlee: Jumping in from SRE — I can see errors hitting the embeddings service from that org id. We're returning dimension_mismatch from the runtime. Logs show model_id: open-embed-medium-1536 in the routing metadata even though the request model field was open-embed-medium-1024. Hash: r12f3. Looks like smart-routing fallback picked a 1536 variant due to capacity.

alex: Ah — that explains it. The runtime did a transparent fallback to a compatible model family but different dimension. We should either (a) fail earlier with a clearer error, or (b) coerce/convert embeddings if we have an upscaling path (we don't). For now the correct workaround is to pin the model variant in the request or disable auto-fallback for embeddings.

maria: How do I pin it? I didn't see that in the quickstart.

docs: I can add a short FAQ + runbook snippet. Quick note to team: our public docs mention model pinning for generation, but embeddings pinning behavior is not well documented — we'll update. Suggested text below.

alex: For immediate repro and workaround, tell the customer to set header X-Redwood-Model-Pin: open-embed-medium-1024 or include \"model: \"open-embed-medium-1024\" and add query ?fallback=false in the HTTP call. Example curl:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings?fallback=false \\\
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' \\\
 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\\
 -d '{"model":"open-embed-medium-1024","input":["..."],"batch_size":4}'
```
This will force a 400 if not available rather than silently routing.

maria: Tried that — now I get a 503 when that exact variant is out of capacity. That's okay, but our pipeline expects consistent dims.

jlee: On throughput: I also noticed some of their calls used batch_size 64 intermittently. Our runtime will auto-split and batch across slots; large batches + fallback produced occasional partial responses where some items got 1536 embeddings, others 1024, leading to downstream consumer errors. We need to recommend a maximum batch_size for embeddings for now.

eng-runtime: For clarity — our runtime can only serve same-dimension embeddings per batch. When fallback occurs mid-batch we should reject the entire request. Looks like we have a bug where split-by-availability logic didn't enforce homogenous dim check. I'll open an eng runtime ticket (RT-6572) to hard-fail.

alex: Thanks. For support steps right now: 1) Ask customer to set fallback=false in query param and pin model; 2) Reduce batch_size to 8 or 16 depending on throughput needs; 3) If they need higher throughput, suggest using our Dedicated capacity which respects pinned variants; 4) We're going to update docs and send a temporary runbook link.

docs: Draft FAQ blurb to add: "Q: Why am I getting dimension_mismatch for embeddings? A: Our runtime may route to compatible model variants if the requested variant is unavailable. Embeddings must have consistent dimensionality — pin your exact model variant and disable automatic fallback (fallback=false) to guarantee consistent output. If you need higher throughput, consider Dedicated capacity or use a model family that shares dims."

maria: Ok please add that to the docs and send a quick example I can paste into our pipeline. Also: is there a recommended way to validate vector dims client-side before indexing?

alex: Recommend client-side assert after the embedding call: if len(vec) != expected_dim: raise and retry with pinned model or backoff. Example snippet: 
```python
resp = client.embeddings.create(model='open-embed-medium-1024', input=[...])
for v in resp['data']:
    if len(v['embedding']) != 1024:
        raise ValueError('dim mismatch')
```
If you see mismatch, do not index the vectors.

support-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-embeddings-dim-mismatch. Linked RT-6572. Pager duty oncall: @jlee.

eng-runtime: We'll prioritize the hard-fail and a short-term mitigation: treat per-request model field as authoritative for routing when embeddings endpoint is used. ETA for patch: 48h.

docs: I'll add the FAQ and a short runbook to internal runbooks page: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/embeddings-troubleshooting (temporary). Will include reproduction steps, sample curl, SDK snippet, and the client-side validation snippet.

maria: Appreciate the fast turnaround. Please ping here when the patch is live so we can remove the fallback=false workaround.

alex: Will do. Assigning follow-up: docs to update public docs + internal runbook (docs), eng-runtime to fix routing hard-fail (eng-runtime), SRE to monitor errors and link to INC (jlee). I'll keep the thread open until patch and doc update are live. :thumbsup:

jlee: Monitoring set: alert when dimension_mismatch rate > 0.1% of embeddings traffic for that org.

alex: Last note for the ticket: logging addition requested — include routed_model_id and requested_model_id in error payload so customers see mismatch reason. eng-runtime can add a short field mismatch_info in the 4xx/5xx responses.

eng-runtime: Acknowledged. We'll add mismatch_info and ensure we never mix dims in a single batch.

maria: Thanks all, holding for the patch.
